plan.notes: Source: official College of Southern Idaho 2024-2025 catalog, 'Agriculture, Associate of Applied Science' program page (Major Code: 4103A), hand-transcribed 2026-10-02 from https://csi.smartcatalogiq.com/en/2024-2025/catalog/agriculture-department/agriculture/agriculture-associate-of-applied-science/ . Transcription method: fetched the official program page and transcribed the four semester tables verbatim (course codes, titles, credits, printed semester totals 14/16/16/14). TRUE award: Associate of Applied Science (page title). Catalog year 2024-2025: the newest CSI catalog with complete published program pages found (a 2025-2026 catalog exists but its program pages were not locatable; the 2024-2025 pages are complete and officially published). Total credits: 60, the catalog's published total ('Total Credit Hours: 60'); semester tables sum 14+16+16+14 = 60. Choice slots: (a) Spring Freshman lists '(AGRI 109 Principles of Animal Science* AND AGRI 109L Lab*) OR (AGRI 120 Science of Animal Husbandry AND AGRI 120L Lab)' - both paths total 4 credits; modeled as one 4-credit choice slot. (b) MATH GE / SOCS GE / COMM GE / SCIG GE are official catalog placeholders for 'any Gen. Ed.' course in that category (student choice). (c) PROG ELEC rows are 'Program Electives' (student choice); the page requires a minimum of 21 credits of program electives for graduation, chosen from the Animal Science / Precision Ag & Agronomy / Natural Resource / Ag. Management pathways printed on the page (or a mix); the four semester blocks (3+2+8+8) sum to 21. Catalog note: 'Neither AGRI 109/109L nor AGRI 110/110L can be used as a program elective if the course is being used to meet the program requirement for this degree.' Variable credit: 'AGRI 227 Agriculture Internship* 3-6 Credits' modeled at 3 credits for the minimum-credit path (2+1+3+8 = 14 matches the printed Spring Sophomore total). Prereqs: left empty. The catalog marks courses with '*' as 'Prerequisite or corequisite required' but does not name the prerequisite on the plan page; per-course prerequisites live on the official catalog course pages, not the plan page. The catalog notes 'Alternative plans of study available by contacting your advisor.'
